title: Guinea’s junta chief elected president after opposition boycott
summary: Mamady Doumbouya reneged on promise not to stand and hand west African country back to civilian ruleThe head of Guinea’s junta, Mamady Doumbouya, who had pledged not to run for office after seizing power four years ago, has been elected president after the country’s electoral commission said he had secured a sweeping majority of the vote.Doumbouya, 41, faced eight rivals for the presidency but the main opposition leaders were barred from running and had urged a boycott of the vote held over the weekend.Continue reading...
